# 3-Week Reconditioning Plan — Summary

## The One-Page Version

Three weeks. Three gym sessions per week. Two runs per week building to three. Every load, every rest day, every cardio session in one place. Use this as the working reference document.

---

## Key Numbers

**Pre-illness 1RMs:** Bench 100 kg | Squat 140 kg | Deadlift 170 kg
**Current bodyweight:** ~81 kg (pre-illness 85 kg)
**Intensity progression:** 50% → 62% → 72% of pre-illness 1RM
**Cardio progression:** 2 × 20–30 min → 2–3 × 30–35 min → 3 × 35–45 min

---

## Week 1 — Re-Sensitisation

**Theme:** Move well, gather information, cost the body nothing it cannot easily repay.

### Loads
| Lift | Load | Sets × Reps |
|---|---|---|
| Squat | 70 kg (50%) | 3 × 10 |
| Bench | 50 kg (50%) | 3 × 10 |
| Deadlift | 85 kg (50%) | 3 × 8 |

### Schedule
| Day | Activity |
|---|---|
| Monday | Gym — Session 1A Lower Body |
| Tuesday | Run 1 — 20–25 min, HR ≤ 130 bpm |
| Wednesday | Gym — Session 1B Upper Body |
| Thursday | Run 2 — 25–30 min, HR ≤ 130 bpm |
| Friday | Gym — Session 1C Full Body / Hinge |
| Saturday | Active recovery — walking and light mobility only |
| Sunday | Full rest |

### Cardio Detail
- Two runs only this week — not three
- Heart rate ceiling 130 bpm throughout — use a monitor
- Run/walk as needed to stay under ceiling — pace is irrelevant
- Time on feet is the metric, not distance
- Expected pace will be significantly slower than pre-illness — this is correct and expected

### Key Rules This Week
- Tempo on all main lifts: 3 seconds down, 1-second pause, 1 second up
- Sessions capped at 60–65 minutes including warm-up
- If energy is poor on Session 1C day, keep deadlift at 85 kg regardless of how earlier sessions went
- End of week check-in: score energy, sleep, soreness, motivation out of 10 — if any score is below 6 consistently, repeat Week 1 before advancing

---

## Week 2 — Load Reintroduction

**Theme:** Add meaningful load, introduce the deadlift as a primary lift, begin to feel like real training again without feeling crushed afterward.

### Loads
| Lift | Load | Sets × Reps |
|---|---|---|
| Squat | 84–88 kg (62%) | 4 × 8 |
| Bench | 62–65 kg (62%) | 4 × 8 |
| Deadlift | 105–110 kg (62%) | 4 × 6 |

### Schedule
| Day | Activity |
|---|---|
| Monday | Gym — Session 2A Lower Body / Squat Focus |
| Tuesday | Run 1 — 30–35 min, HR ≤ 135 bpm |
| Wednesday | Gym — Session 2B Upper Body / Bench Focus |
| Thursday | Run 2 — 30–35 min, HR ≤ 135 bpm |
| Friday | Gym — Session 2C Full Body / Deadlift Focus |
| Saturday | Optional Run 3 — 25–30 min easy, HR ≤ 130 bpm, only if both earlier runs felt good and recovery is solid |
| Sunday | Full rest |

### Cardio Detail
- Two runs guaranteed, third run optional and conditional on recovery quality
- Heart rate ceiling rises slightly to 135 bpm
- Pace should be improving relative to Week 1 at the same heart rate — if it is not, the body is still recovering and loads may need reviewing
- Still no pace targets — effort and heart rate govern everything
- If Saturday run is taken, Sunday must be complete rest with no exceptions

### Key Rules This Week
- Tempo relaxes slightly — 2 seconds down, 1-second pause, 1 second up on main lifts
- Watch for lower back fatigue on bent-over rows — form breakdown here is an early fatigue signal
- Farmer's carries introduced in Session 2C — start with a load that allows tall posture and no lateral sway
- 48-hour post-session check: if soreness from Session 2A is still significant on Wednesday, reduce Session 2B loads by 5% and flag it
- End of week check-in: same 1–10 scoring — all markers should be trending upward from Week 1

---

## Week 3 — Baseline Approach

**Theme:** Bridge week. Loads reach 70–75%, rep ranges tighten, sessions resemble pre-illness training. Ends with a conservative 1RM assessment to reset the programme off real numbers.

### Loads
| Lift | Load | Sets × Reps |
|---|---|---|
| Squat | 98–105 kg (72%) | 4 × 5 |
| Bench | 70–75 kg (72%) | 4 × 5 |
| Deadlift | 119–127 kg (72%) | 4 × 5 |

### Schedule
| Day | Activity |
|---|---|
| Monday | Gym — Session 3A Lower Body / Squat Focus |
| Tuesday | Run 1 — 35–40 min, HR ≤ 140 bpm |
| Wednesday | Gym — Session 3B Upper Body / Bench Focus |
| Thursday | **Full rest — no running, no gym, no active recovery beyond walking** |
| Friday | **1RM Assessment Session** |
| Saturday | Active recovery — walking only |
| Sunday | Full rest |

### Cardio Detail
- Three runs this week — Tuesday, and two further runs to be placed on non-gym, non-assessment days according to the client's schedule
- Heart rate ceiling rises to 140 bpm
- One of the three runs should include a **10-minute controlled tempo section** in the middle — settle into easy pace for 10–12 minutes, lift to a comfortably hard effort for 10 minutes, return to easy pace for the remainder
- By end of Week 3 he should be completing 35–45 minutes continuously without walk breaks
- Target for full 10k return: Week 4–5, not this week

### 1RM Assessment Session — Friday

**Pre-conditions — postpone if any are not met:**
- Resting HR within normal range Friday morning
- No significant soreness from Session 3B
- 7+ hours sleep Wednesday and Thursday nights
- Morning energy score 7 or above
- Well hydrated, proper meal 2–3 hours before session

**Order:** Squat → Bench → Deadlift. Minimum 10–12 minutes between lifts.

**Attempt Structure:**

| Lift | Attempt 1 | Attempt 2 | Attempt 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Squat | 115 kg | 122–125 kg | 128–132 kg |
| Bench | 82–85 kg | 88–90 kg | 93–95 kg |
| Deadlift | 142–145 kg | 150–153 kg | 157–160 kg |

**Rules for all three lifts:**
- Maximum three attempts per lift — no exceptions
- Advance to next attempt only if previous attempt was clean technique and RPE 8 or below
- A slow grind is not a number to programme from — stop at the last clean rep
- Deadlift rules are strictest — any lower back fatigue or tightness from squat work means stopping at Attempt 1

**Expected results and estimated 1RMs:**
| Lift | Expected Best Single | Estimated 1RM |
|---|---|---|
| Squat | 125–130 kg | 131–140 kg |
| Bench | 90–93 kg | 94–100 kg |
| Deadlift | 150–155 kg | 157–167 kg |

---

## Nutrition Targets — All Three Weeks

| | Week 1 | Week 2 | Week 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Calories | 2,900–3,000 | 3,000–3,100 | 3,100–3,200 |
| Protein | 170 g | 175 g | 180 g |
| Carbohydrates | 340 g | 360 g | 375 g |
| Fat | 90 g | 92 g | 95 g |

- Protein distributed across 4–5 meals — 35–45 g per sitting
- Carbohydrates prioritised around training — 50–70 g pre-session, 60–80 g post-session
- Casein protein or cottage cheese before bed every night
- 3.0–4.0 litres of water daily — more on training days
- Creatine 3–5 g daily, fish oil 2–3 g EPA/DHA, vitamin D 2,000–4,000 IU, magnesium glycinate 300–400 mg before bed

---

## Readiness Signals — When He Is Ready for Full Intensity

Clear all of the following before advancing to pre-illness loads:

**Must be green before Week 4 full intensity:**
- Resting HR within 3–5 bpm of baseline for 5+ consecutive mornings
- Morning energy consistently 7+ for 5+ consecutive days
- Post-session soreness resolving within 48 hours after all Week 3 sessions
- Sleep quality consistently good — falling asleep easily, waking refreshed
- Bar speed improving week on week at prescribed loads
- RPE at 70–75% loads sitting at 6–7, not 8–9
- No post-exertional energy crashes after any Week 3 session
- Bodyweight trending back toward pre-illness weight
- Running HR at easy pace within 5–8 bpm of pre-illness baseline

**If any signal is amber:** Extend reconditioning by one week at Week 3 loads before testing or advancing.

---

## Week 4 Opening Loads — Off Test Numbers

Programme Week 4 at **80% of estimated 1RMs from the assessment session**, not 80% of pre-illness numbers.

| Lift | Estimated 1RM from Test | Week 4 Opening Load |
|---|---|---|
| Squat | ~132 kg | ~105 kg |
| Bench | ~93 kg | ~74 kg |
| Deadlift | ~159 kg | ~127 kg |

Return to pre-illness 1RMs expected within **3–5 weeks** of Week 4. Surpassing pre-illness numbers expected within **8–10 weeks** with consistent training, nutrition, and recovery.

---

## The Non-Negotiables Across All Three Weeks

- Sessions never exceed 65 minutes including warm-up
- 48-hour post-session response monitored after every session — disproportionate fatigue or soreness means holding loads, not advancing
- Running always on rest days from the gym — never on the same day as a gym session
- Thursday of Week 3 is complete rest regardless of how good he feels — the assessment session requires a fresh nervous system
- If he reports feeling worse after a session than before it on two or more occasions in any week, that week's loads are repeated before advancing
- Pre-illness loads are not attempted until the readiness checklist above is fully green
